summary: Three independent attempts to fix the Part-2 ShareRobot direction problem, all falsified the duplicated-history hypothesis as the sole cause.

attempt_2_H3_real_frames_noisy_depth.result: zero motion predicted (model likely distrusted an implausible 3D history)

attempt_3_H3_real_frames_consistent_dept.depth: single t0 depth map reused for all 3 frames (physically consistent)
attempt_3_H3_real_frames_consistent_dept.note: predicted direction is close to OPPOSITE the real history direction it was just given

conclusion: Across 3 independently-constructed real (non-duplicated) history inputs, direction prediction is never reliably correct (cosine ranges -0.60 to -0.62, one case exactly opposite its own input history at -0.97). This is not explained by duplicated history (falsified: attempts 2-3 used real history) or by depth noise alone (falsified: attempt 3 fixed depth consistency and still got the wrong direction). Most likely a genuine domain-transfer limitation: invented camera intrinsics, an action-conditioning phrasing unlike the training distribution, and/or a training distribution dominated by outdoor/tracked-object motion (DAVIS-style) rather than tabletop robot manipulation.
